During the battle, the Moff ordered his men to fire the battle station's [[Superlaser/Legends|superlaser]] at the Rebel fleet, destroying several of their capital ships. Jerjerrod later positioned the Death Star to destroy Endor's forest moon, remembering Palpatine's orders to destroy it if the Rebels brought down the shield. However, before he could carry out that order, he was killed when the Death Star was destroyed by the Alliance.<ref name="ROTJ" />

[[File:IG-88headshot.jpg|thumb|right|65px|IG-88A]]

The first of the IG-88 [[Assassin droid/Legends|assassin droids]], IG-88A gained a strong level of sentience and planned to launch a droid revolution against the [[Human/Legends|Human]]-controlled Galactic Empire. After all the other IG-88 units were destroyed, IG-88A gained access to the computer core inside the Death Star II, and controlled the battle station's weapon systems. While the Empire was unaware that he was actually controlling the Death Star, Palpatine was suspicious when several of the doors in his throne room mysteriously opened and closed. When the Rebels destroyed the Death Star, IG-88A was obliterated, and both his body and consciousness were destroyed. As a result, his planned revolution never occurred.<ref name="TIA:TTOIG88" />

====Luke Skywalker====
[[File:LukeSkywalker-RotJAVA.png|thumb|right|65px|Luke Skywalker]]
{{Main|Luke Skywalker/Legends}}
A Jedi Knight and hero of the Rebel Alliance, Luke Skywalker was shocked when he learned of his identity as the son of Darth Vader. During the Battle of Endor, he was part of the Rebel strike force that descended to the forest moon of Endor. While there, he revealed to Leia Organa that the two of them were siblings. He then left to surrender to Vader, who had come looking for him, in order to protect his friends. On board the Death Star, Darth Sidious attempted to turn Luke to the dark side of the Force, and had Luke duel his father. Finally, Vader saved his son by killing the Emperor, and redeemed himself, telling Luke that he had been right all along. Skywalker escaped the exploding battle station with his father's body, and though he was saddened by his father's passing, he joined the Rebel celebration on Endor that night.<ref name="ROTJ" /> He would go on to serve the New Republic<ref name="Heir to the Empire">''[[Heir to the Empire]]''</ref> and form the New Jedi Order, achieving his destiny.<ref name="Jedi vs. Sith" />

====General Han Solo====
[[File:HanSolo-Headshot-New.jpg|thumb|right|65px|Han Solo]]

After arriving on Endor, Han, Luke, Leia, Chewbacca, R2-D2, and C-3PO met the native Ewoks and gained their help. Solo and his group infiltrated the [[Deflector shield generator/Legends|shield generator]] bunker, and after a skirmish during which the Ewoks helped the Rebels, the Death Star's shield was brought down, allowing Calrissian and the others to attack the [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]]. Following its destruction, Han Solo celebrated with the rest of the Rebels in Bright Tree Village. He learned from Leia Organa that Luke Skywalker was her brother, which allowed him to continue his love affair with her.<ref name="ROTJ" /> Later, he served the New Republic, continuing what he accomplished at Endor.<ref name="Heir to the Empire" />

====Leia Organa====
[[File:Leia_endorpromo02.jpg|thumb|right|65px|Leia Organa]]

An [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaanian]] [[Prince/Legends|princess]],<ref name="ROTJn" /> Leia Organa became one of the Rebel Alliance's most important fighters. [[File:Wicket_RotJ.png|thumb|right|65px|Wicket W. Warrick]]
{{Main|Wicket Wystri Warrick/Legends}}
A scout from the Bright Tree Village Ewok tribe on Endor's forest moon, Wicket encountered the members of the Rebel Alliance during the early stages of the Battle of Endor. While on patrol through the forest, Wicket encountered Leia Organa, who had been injured during a speeder bike pursuit, and befriended the Human woman. During the ensuing battle on Endor's surface, Wicket rallied his fellow Ewoks from Bright Tree Village to fight alongside the Rebels. {{Main|Lando Calrissian/Legends}}
A smuggler, [[Gambling/Legends|gambler]], and friend of Han Solo, Lando Calrissian followed in his friend's footsteps and joined the Rebel Alliance. During the Battle of Endor, he was promoted to the rank of general by the Alliance. He was assigned to pilot Solo's ship, the ''Millennium Falcon'', which had been his in the past. Lando flew in the space battle while Solo led the ground assault. He fought with the Alliance Fleet in orbit of Endor, but he, along with the other Rebels, realized that the battle had been a trap, as the Death Star's weapon systems were already operational. Calrissian flew in the desperate fight, but when Solo's team on the ground brought down the Death Star's shield, things turned better for the Alliance. However, he soon discovered that the battle was a trap by the Empire, as the Death Star's weapon systems were already in operation, even though the Rebels had believed the opposite. Soon after, Lando Calrissian and Wedge Antilles destroyed the Death Star from the inside, leading the Alliance to a nearly impossible victory.<ref name="ROTJ" /> Being hailed as one of the battle's many heroes, Ackbar would go on to serve the New Republic for over two decades.<ref name="NEGTC" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Battle of Endor acted as the climax for the [[1983]] film [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']],<ref name="ROTJ" /> the concluding installment of the [[original trilogy]].

===Development===
For the ground-based part of the battle, series creator [[George Lucas]] decided to make Ewoks the primitive race that aided the Rebellion instead of Wookiees because the previous movies had already established Chewbacca to be technologically proficient.<ref name="commentary">{{HomeVideoCite|set=Star Wars Trilogy (DVD)|episode=Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|etext=''Return of the Jedi''}}</ref>

Because he specifically wanted a primitive race with no prior ties to technology to be the ultimate victor of the battle, and partially to make the film more marketable for kids, he created the Ewok race and had them effectively win the ground portion of the battle. This decision was controversial to both the actors and some fans. Lucas was inspired to have a primitive race win against an advanced army from the actions of the [[Wikipedia:Viet Cong|Vietcong]], and also used the battle as a way of commenting on United States involvement in the [[Wikipedia:Vietnam War|Vietnam War]].<ref name="EoD">''[[Empire of Dreams: The Story of the Star Wars Trilogy]]''</ref> The inspiration, when it came to light, led to further controversy, as it implied that the Galactic Empire represented the American forces.

Of the part of the battle taking place in the throne room, ''Return of the Jedi'' director [[Richard Marquand]] said that Lucas wanted the duel to be bigger than the Duel on Cloud City but changed his mind during shooting, saying: "George is very blunt. He said, 'It's just a couple of guys banging sticks against each other. Don't worry about that. It is bigger because of what is going on in their heads.{{' "}}<ref name="SWArchive-Degrees of Confrontation">{{SWArchive|url=episode-vi/explore/classic/2000/04/classic20000424.html|text=Episode VI Classic Moment - Degrees of Confrontation}}</ref>

A deleted scene expanded a bit on the actions inside the bunker during the second attempt: Specifically, where Han Solo and his unit encountered a stormtrooper squad inside the control room. Said event eventually appeared during gameplay in ''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike]]''.

===Later insights===
The [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi (junior novelization)|junior novelization of ''Return of the Jedi'']], written after completion of the [[prequel trilogy]], relates Vader's thoughts as he watches Palpatine torture Luke, and suggests that the thought of Padmé and her love broke through to him, and that knowing it was ''her'' son being tortured that restored Anakin and compelled him to turn on the Emperor. ''[[The Life and Legend of Obi-Wan Kenobi]]'' describes Obi-Wan watching the duel from the [[Netherworld of the Force/Legends|netherworld of the Force]]. Once Luke refuses to kill Vader and the lightning attack begins, looking on in horror as Luke, and with him the hope of the Jedi, is destroyed by the Dark Lord of the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]], Kenobi can hardly believe his eyes when the friend he had given up on as hopelessly enthralled by the dark side reasserts himself and saves his son.

[[Lawrence Kasdan]] says: "My sense of the relationship between Vader and the Emperor is that the Emperor is much more powerful than Vader and that Vader is very much intimidated by him. Vader has dignity, but the Emperor in ''Jedi'' really has all the power."<ref name="SWArchive-Who has the Power?">{{SWArchive|url=episode-vi/explore/classic/2000/02/classic20000228.html|text=Episode VI Classic Moment - Who has the Power?}}</ref>

The fate of the Ewoks has been discussed in the Endor Holocaust theory, which states that Endor, along with the Ewoks on it, was inevitably destroyed by falling debris from the Death Star.<ref name="Fury" /><ref name="Xw:WG" /> This theory has been asserted by [[Curtis Saxton]]'s [[Curtis Saxton|Star Wars Technical Commentaries]] website,<ref name="Tech">[[Curtis Saxton|Star Wars Technical Commentaries]]</ref> but has been refuted by subsequent source materials, such as [[Pablo Hidalgo]]'s explanation in a question-and-answer column of [[Star Wars Insider 76|''Star Wars Insider'' 76]]. Hidalgo asserted that a hyperspace wormhole transported debris from the Endor system to the other side of the galaxy, as with [[Glove of Darth Vader|Darth Vader's glove]] in ''[[The Glove of Darth Vader]]''.<ref name="Glove">''[[The Glove of Darth Vader]]''</ref> Hidalgo also argues that the laws of physics can be put aside in this case because George Lucas wanted the story to end well for the protagonists.<ref name="In76">[[Star Wars Insider 76|''Star Wars Insider'' 76]]</ref> Two of the ''[[Star Wars: Legacy of the Force]]'' novels are set on Endor; these show the moon and its inhabitants as fine, with only limited damage to their habitats.<ref name="Fury" /><ref name="Revelation" />

===Different portrayals===
{{Quote|Congratulations, commander, you've managed to defend the shield generator and thwart the plans of the Rebel Alliance. A statue will be erected of you on the planet Coruscant.|Darth Vader to the player at the end of the Endor simulation|<ref name="SW:GB" />}}
[[File:Rs2_endor.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The view of the battle from the cockpit of Wedge Antilles' X-wing after the Imperial Fleet springs its ambush]]
The battle was introduced in the [[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (novelization)|''Return of the Jedi'' novelization]], which contained slight discrepancies from the film, as did some other spin-off materials. Also, the re-releases of the original trilogy made some minor alterations to certain scenes, including those from the Battle of Endor. While most were trivial changes in color, sound effects, or music,<ref name="Special Edition">[[The Star Wars Trilogy Special Edition]]</ref> very brief scenes of celebrations were added to the end, and Anakin Skywalker's Force ghost was changed from [[Sebastian Shaw]]'s face to that of [[Hayden Christensen]],<ref name="DVD">[[Star Wars Trilogy (DVD)|''Star Wars Trilogy'' DVD]]</ref> who portrayed Anakin in the prequels.<ref name="ROTS" /> [[Lucasfilm]] has stated that the [[2004]] [[Star Wars Trilogy (DVD)|DVD versions]] are the [[canon]]ical depiction of the events in the trilogy, including the Battle of Endor.<ref name="Blog">{{Blog|bachsolosblog|14|Bach Solo's Blog: Unaltered OT On DVD! What Does This Mean For You?|nobackup=1}}</ref>

[[File:MCQ-mccruiser.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Concept art of the space battle by [[Ralph McQuarrie]]]]
The battle presented in ''Return of the Jedi'' inspired many other spin-off materials, including television series<ref name="Ewoks">[[Ewoks (television series)|''Ewoks'']]</ref> and [[Star Wars video games|video game]]s.<ref name="RS" /><ref name="ES" /> Many characters with only brief appearances in the movie were given names and backstories.<ref name="Endor Limited" /> The Ewoks received much attention, spawning a [[Ewoks (television series)|television series]], as well as two TV movies, ''[[Caravan of Courage: An Ewok Adventure]]'' and ''[[Ewoks: The Battle for Endor]]''.

The Battle of Endor was also reflected in various toys, such as a large [[LEGO Star Wars|LEGO ''Star Wars'']] playset,<ref name="LEGO Dictionary">''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> as well as numerous video games, such as [[Star Wars: X-Wing Alliance|''X-Wing Alliance'']] and [[Star Wars: Force Commander|''Force Commander'']]. ''[[Star Wars: Battlefront]]'' and [[Star Wars: Battlefront II|''Battlefront II'']] allowed gamers to replay the battle as they wished, therefore making its portrayal non-canon. ''[[Star Wars Battlefront: Renegade Squadron]]'', released in [[2007]], and its [[2009]] sequel, [[Star Wars Battlefront: Elite Squadron|''Elite Squadron'']], both had Endor missions in their campaigns. These showed the battle from different viewpoints, the first from Col Serra's Renegade Squadron and the second from X2, with the objectives in both paralleling the events in ''Return of the Jedi''.<ref name="RS" /><ref name="ES" /> ''[[LEGO Star Wars II: The Original Trilogy]]'' and its remake, [[LEGO Star Wars: The Complete Saga|''The Complete Saga'']], both had four missions related to the Battle of Endor, though the portrayal of the events varied from that of the film. Because the events in the game are treated with a humorous approach and do not strictly follow the story,<ref name="LEGO Star Wars II">''[[LEGO Star Wars II: The Original Trilogy]]''</ref><ref name="The Complete Saga">''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Complete Saga]]''</ref> this article assumes that they are non-canon.

[[File:LEGORebelCelebration.png|thumb|left|300px|The heroes of Endor as LEGO minifigures]]
The [[2001]] video game ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]'' offered two versions of the Battle of Endor, one in the Leia Organa (Rebel/New Republic) campaign and the other one in the Darth Vader (Imperial) campaign. The latter was an alternate-history version narrated by Mara Jade. The player was given a large army and tasked with defending the shield generator from Rebel and Ewok forces. After 15 minutes of real-time play, the scenario ends, and the "commander" is promised a [[Statuary|statue]] on Coruscant. The Rebel mission followed the movie version more closely. The player was given 18 troopers and 2 [[2-1C medical droid|medics]], along with Organa, Solo, and C-3PO. The force advanced and met Wicket, then fought through a stormtrooper camp. At the next base the force destroyed a [[command center]]. After that base they came to the Ewok village and gained reinforcements, including Chewbacca in an AT-ST. The force then advanced toward the shield generator bunker, entered it, and destroyed it. The game's [[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds: Prima's Official Strategy Guide|strategy guide]] recommends for the Imperial campaign that the player push back quickly against the stream of attackers. For the Rebel mission, the guide recommends using the Ewok gliders once they join the team to scout ahead and destroy turrets. The missions were also included in the game's [[2002]] expansion pack, ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds: Clone Campaigns]]''.<ref name="SW:GB" />

The Battle of Endor also made a frequent appearance in the [[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron (series)|''Star Wars: Rogue Squadron'' series]] of video games, mostly as the final missions of the campaign. In [[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron II: Rogue Leader|''Rogue Leader'']], in addition to [[Battle of Kothlis|four]] [[Mission to Prefsbelt IV|different]] [[Raid on Bespin|missions]] that led up to the Battle of Endor, the battle itself was the focus of two different missions. The first, titled "Battle of Endor," focused on the initial stages of the space battle. The second, "Strike at the Core," focused on the primary objective of pushing towards the reactor core and destroying it. In ''Rebel Strike'', like in ''Rogue Leader'', the final missions focused on the Battle of Endor. In this case, however, the missions, referred to collectively as the Endor campaign on the mission selection menu, focused on the ground aspects. The first mission, "Speeder Bike Pursuit," focused on Luke and Leia's attempts to stop several scout troopers from reporting their presence on Endor, and ends when Luke kills the last scout with a lightsaber, as in the movie. The second mission, "Triumph of the Rebellion," focused on the ground battle proper, specifically on Chewbacca's traveling to aid the Rebels at the bunker after hijacking an AT-ST, then Han Solo's setting of detonation charges and his final battle with Sarkli. In addition to the two main missions, the Endor campaign in the same game included a bonus mission called "Attack on the ''Executor''." As the title suggests, it focused on the events between Admiral Ackbar's order to attack the ''Executor'' to buy Calrissian more time and the destruction of the ''Executor''. "Attack on the ''Executor''" was also the only bonus mission in the single-player mode of ''Rebel Strike'' to not include footage taken directly from the film. Instead, it utilized its own cinematics. Aside from this, both the Luke and Wedge campaigns ended with a direct lead-in to the Endor campaign (the former via the [[Battle of the Great Pit of Carkoon]] and the latter via the [[Fondor shipyard assault]], the latter of which had an indirect reference to the Battle of Endor via the debriefing between Vader and Palpatine where the latter implies he deliberately allowed the Rebels to destroy the prototype cloaking device-equipped ''Executor'' star dreadnought specifically to make them overconfident and have them walk right into his trap).

The [[Wikipedia:Super Nintendo Entertainment System|Super Nintendo Entertainment System]] game ''[[Super Star Wars: Return of the Jedi]]'' featured the Death Star duel, although with a few differences: Vader ambushes Luke via a door and also utilizes Force Flight to a degree, and Luke duels Emperor Palpatine instead of simply being tortured by him as in the movie. In addition, Palpatine during the battle also utilizes Force Flight throughout the later portion of the battle, with him falling into the reactor after Luke defeated him as a result. Despite this, Vader was redeemed to some extent due to it using his final moments as well as the presence of his Force ghost.

Author [[Timothy Zahn]] stated that in his opinion, if Grand Admiral Thrawn had been in command during the Battle of Endor, the result would almost certainly have been a Rebel loss.<ref name="Heir 20">''[[Heir to the Empire: The 20th Anniversary Edition]]''</ref>

====''Infinities''====
Another non-canon portrayal of the battle occurred in the comic ''[[Star Wars Infinities: Return of the Jedi]]'', which rewrote the events of the film in an alternate scenario. While this storyline involves the same characters, locations, and battles as the movie, the plot is altered.

In this version, Luke was captured by the Empire after leaving Dagobah and after he left two messages: one to tell Leia that they are brother and sister and that Vader is their father, and another to the Rebel fleet not to rescue him. Leia goes to the Death Star to rescue him but is captured and brought to the Emperor.

A group of Rebels lands on Endor and destroys the shield generator. Han Solo is unfrozen from carbonite aboard the ''Home One'' and mans the turrets on the ''Millennium Falcon'' while still blind.

Aboard the Death Star, Palpatine orders Vader to kill Leia, but Luke blocks Vader's strike and duels him. Luke swings an attack to Vader's legs, but Vader jumps and kicks him in the face. Palpatine gives one last chance to join him or die. Leia attempts to intervene, but Palpatine subdues her with Force lightning. Luke says he doesn't want to fight anymore and asks Vader if he can kill both of his children, and Vader and Palpatine are stunned by the revelation. Not swayed by Luke's proposal of trying to pull him from the dark side, Vader continues the fight.

When Wedge Antilles and the X-wings under his command destroy the Death Star's reactor core, Palpatine escapes, and Luke cuts Vader's right arm off. But the Dark Lord is still powerful enough to use the Force to summon his lightsaber to his left hand and bring Luke to his knees. Luke says he will not fight anymore, and says that if he wants to strike both him and Leia down, he should do so now, but doesn't believe he will. Instead, Vader falls to his knees and begs forgiveness, causing him to turn from the dark side of the Force and become Anakin once again, whereupon he changes to an all-white version of his armor.

The Rebels, along with the redeemed Anakin, go on a mission to stop the escaped Palpatine.<ref name="Infinities">''[[Star Wars Infinities: Return of the Jedi]]''</ref>

====''The Force Unleashed II'': The Battle of Endor====
{{Quote|A great day, Lord Vader. Today marks the death of the Rebellion, and the birth of a new era of peace for the Empire. There is but one last detail to take care of. Do you take me for a fool? Your feeble schemes to overthrow me, using that pathetic clone of your former apprentice, were pitifully obvious from their inception. Now, ''Skywalker'', you will die.|Emperor Palpatine, to Darth Vader|<ref name="DLC">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II]]'' DLC</ref>}}
[[File:TFU2_TBoE_DLC.png|thumb|right|250px|The Dark Apprentice fighting Rebel forces]]
The video game ''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II]]'' includes a downloadable bonus level, featuring a non-canon version of the Battle of Endor. Darth Vader's [[Dark Apprentice]], the only stable clone of Galen Marek, travels in secret to Endor with orders to thwart the Rebel attack on the Imperial shield generator bunker. After landing the ''[[Rogue Shadow]]'' on the forest moon, the apprentice makes his way to the bunker's secret entrance, killing numerous Rebels and Ewoks along the way. Han Solo and Chewbacca also die by the Dark Apprentice's hand just before he enters the base.<ref name="DLC" />

The remaining Rebels are caught in a firefight with the bunker's [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial guards]]. The apprentice kills everyone in his path before finally confronting Princess Leia Organa, who reveals herself to be a [[Jedi training/Legends|trained Jedi]] due to her twin brother's death in the Battle of Hoth. Wielding a yellow-bladed lightsaber, the [[Jedi Princess]] engages her Sith nemesis, and although Organa impresses him with her combat skills and Force potential, she is ultimately outmatched by the more experienced Sith apprentice. Organa makes her final stand at the top of the [[SLD-26 planetary shield generator/Legends|SLD-26 planetary shield generator]], where she dies after the apprentice fatally [[Shiak|stabs]] her through the abdomen with one of his dual lightsabers, thus ending the duel and the Alliance's only chance to destroy the second Death Star.<ref name="DLC" />

In the incomplete [[Battle station/Legends|battle station's]] [[Mooring tower/Legends|mooring tower]] throne room, Emperor Palpatine and Darth Vader are observing the space battle outside the circular viewport. As the Galactic Empire prevails over its enemies, Palpatine declares that the Rebellion has been destroyed, allowing the Empire to return to a state of peace. However, he also uses this moment to reveal how he knew about the secret cloning project on [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]], and more specifically, Vader's plot to overthrow the Emperor by utilizing the dark clone of the original apprentice as an asset. As such, the Emperor threatens to execute Vader for [[Treason/Legends|treason]], mockingly calling him "Skywalker." Vader activates his lightsaber, but is unable to defend himself against his Master's Force lightning attack. Defeated and on his knees, Vader can do nothing to stop Palpatine from dispatching Captain Sarkli and his [[Troop/Legends|troops]] to kill the clone.<ref name="DLC" />

Meanwhile, the Dark Apprentice sits in [[Meditation/Legends|meditation]] with Leia Organa's corpse nearby. As a group of [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer/Legends|Imperial Star Destroyers]] approaches his position, the clone opens his eyes, both of which reflect his extreme immersion within the dark side of the Force.<ref name="DLC" />

===The story after Endor===
While the Battle of Endor concludes both the original ''[[Star Wars]]'' trilogy and the ''Star Wars'' movie saga in the [[Star Wars Legends|Legends]] continuity,<ref name="ROTJ" /> it did not end the whole ''Star Wars'' story. George Lucas, who constantly denied any possibility of any future movies,<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://www.killermovies.com/s/starwarsepisodeiii/articles/4415.html|text=George Lucas Talks On 'Star Wars' Sequels 7, 8 & 9|work=[http://www.killermovies.com KillerMovies.com]|archivedate=20200505171158}}</ref> affirmed his belief that the saga ends with the death of Anakin Skywalker, since he was the tragic hero.<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://www.cinematical.com/2008/05/07/will-lucas-extend-his-star-wars-story-past-return-of-the-je|text=Will Lucas Extend His 'Star Wars' Story Beyond 'Return of the Jedi'?|work=[http://www.cinematical.com Cinematical.com]|archivedate=20080510084717}}</ref> However, countless Expanded Universe stories told what happened to the Rebels and the Imperials in the post-Endor years. ''[[The Truce at Bakura]]'', released in [[1994]], detailed the events in the aftermath of the Battle of Endor;<ref name="Truce" /> so did the [[Marvel Comics|Marvel]] ''Star Wars'' [[Star Wars comic books|comics]].<ref name="Star Wars 100" /> [[Star Wars: The Thrawn Trilogy|''The Thrawn Trilogy'']], beginning in [[1991]] and ending in [[1993]], showed the continuing war five years after the Battle of Endor, with the New Republic fighting the newly ignited force of the Empire.<ref name="Heir to the Empire" /><ref name="The Last Command">''[[The Last Command]]''</ref> Many later works introduced more post-Endor stories, including Palpatine's resurrection as a clone<ref name="EE2" /><ref name="DE2" /> and Luke Skywalker's founding of the [[New Jedi Order]], and the conflicts and challenges facing it.<ref name="Jedi vs. Sith" /> For both the Battle of Endor and all other events in the ''Star Wars'' movies, the film continuity and the Expanded Universe material have been meshed together to form part of the whole ''Star Wars'' epic.<ref name="Blog-holocron|33">{{Blog|holocron|33|What'd I say again? Select posts by me regarding continuity}}</ref>

This, however, was not to last: the reboot of the canon in April [[2014]] ([[2012|two years after]] Disney bought Lucasfilm and the rights to ''Star Wars'') rendered the Expanded Universe non-canon.<ref name="Legends">{{SW|url=news/the-legendary-star-wars-expanded-universe-turns-a-new-page|text=The Legendary Star Wars Expanded Universe Turns a New Page}}</ref> The ''Star Wars'' [[sequel trilogy]], released between [[2015]] and [[2019]], provided the new canonical account of the story past the Battle of Endor.<ref name="Episode VII">{{Film|VII}}</ref><ref name="Episode VIII">{{Film|VIII}}</ref><ref name="Episode IX">{{Film|IX}}</ref>
